1741.title: Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission
1741.court: Supreme Court of the United States

texts.1741: Due consideration leads to this conclusion: Austin, 494 U. S. 652, should be and now is overruled. We return to the principle established in Buckley and Bellotti that the Government may not suppress political speech on the basis of the speaker's corporate identity. Austin is overruled, so it provides no basis for allowing the Government to limit corporate independent expenditures. Given our conclusion we are further required to overrule the part of McConnell that upheld BCRA §203's extension of §441b's restrictions on corporate independent expenditures.
